ety.text: From Middle English allone, from earlier all oon (literally “all one”), contracted from the Old English phrase eall ān (“completely alone”), equivalent to al- (“all”) + one. Cognate with Scots alane (“alone”), Saterland Frisian alleene (“alone”), West Frisian allinne (“alone”), Dutch alleen (“alone”), Low German alleen (“alone”), German allein (“alone”), Danish alene (“alone”), Swedish allena (“alone”). More at all and one. For the different phonological development of alone and one, see the note in one.

ex: I can't ask for help because I am alone.
It is not good that the man should be alone.

senses.d: Not involved in a romantic relationship.

senses.d: Apart from, or exclusive of, others.
ex: God, […] by whose alone power and conversation we all live, and move, and have our being.

senses.d: By oneself; apart from, or exclusive of, others; solo.
